emerald.note: Brand and signal color in one. Named for CRT phosphor. It is the brand color and is meant to be used freely, not rationed; the binding constraint is AA contrast where it carries text or iconography.

emerald-muted.note: Accent at 15% for chip and badge fills. Sibling washes: 0.20 selection, 0.08 accent glow, 0.07 highlighted code line, 0.04 blockquote fill.

deep.note: Page ground and the inside of every code and media frame. Nothing sits behind it.

surface.note: Step 2 of the tonal ladder: cards, controls, and chips at rest.

surface-2.note: Step 3 of the tonal ladder: hover, active, and raised states.

foreground.note: Headings and primary text. Deliberately not pure white — large type would vibrate against near-black.

muted-foreground.note: Body copy and captions; carries most of the reading load. Steps down via /60, /50, /40, /30 for chrome and idle icons.

border.note: Every default edge. Brightens to 0.12 on hover and 0.20 on active or focused controls.

destructive.note: Destructive and invalid states only. Present in the component layer, effectively unused on the marketing surface.

muted-dim.note: Tertiary text floor. Replaces the muted-foreground/30..70 opacity variants; clears AA 4.5:1 on deep (6.61), surface (5.88) and surface-2 (4.95).

display.purpose: Hero and page headlines. One per page, always tightened to -0.03em.

body.purpose: Descriptions and article prose in Contact Sheet Grey. Drops to 1rem/1.8 below 768px.

label.purpose: The .mono-label eyebrow — uppercase, 0.1em tracked, mint. The system's most recognizable typographic signature.

code.purpose: Terminal output, install commands, code samples, and frame captions.

shadows.name: accent-glow
shadows.purpose: The only shadow token in the system. A wide, very low-opacity mint bloom behind accent elements. Mint rather than black because it represents emitted light, not a cast shadow.

motion.name: ease-expo-out
motion.purpose: The system's reveal ease. Framer Motion variants use it for all entrance animation.

motion.name: duration-reveal
motion.purpose: Framer Motion reveal: opacity 0->1 with a 16px rise (20px lateral for directional variants).

motion.name: stagger-children
motion.purpose: Child stagger interval, with a 40ms delayChildren lead-in.

motion.name: duration-state
motion.purpose: Default transition for hover, focus, and color state changes.

motion.name: parallax-hero
motion.purpose: Hero frame yPercent drift, scrub-linked. Deliberately barely perceptible.

containers.name: wide
containers.purpose: Galleries and comparison views that need to breathe.

containers.name: chrome
containers.purpose: Nav bar and hero media frame (max-w-6xl).

narrative.overview:
Stormlog's interface is a controlled dark space where evidence develops and becomes legible. The product exists because a training run died at 3am and left nothing behind; the site's job is to be the room where you go afterward and look carefully at what happened. That makes it forensic rather than promotional. Surfaces are quiet and near-black so the artifact under examination — a TUI capture, a code block, a memory reading — is the brightest thing on screen. Nothing competes with the evidence.

The system is dark-only by construction. :root and .dark resolve to identical values, so there is no light mode to design for and no theme-toggle branch to reason about; the darkness is a material fact, not a user preference. Depth comes from a three-step tonal ladder rather than shadow — deep (#09090b) for the page ground, surface (#18181b) for cards and controls, surface-2 (#27272a) for raised and hovered states — reinforced by hairline borders at 6% white. A single mint accent carries brand and signal. Monospace is a first-class voice, not a code-block afterthought: eyebrow labels, version chips, frame captions, and install commands all speak in JetBrains Mono, because the product's native habitat is a terminal and the site does not translate that away.

Restraint is doing real work here, so the rejections are as load-bearing as the rules. This is not a dark SaaS page: no gradient meshes, no glowing orbs, no aurora blurs, no gradient text. Not glassmorphism: the nav's backdrop blur is functional legibility, not a decorative material to spread. Not a consumer app: no mascots, illustrations, pastels, or playful microcopy. Not enterprise stock: no laptop photography, no abstract 3D, no logo wall of customers that do not exist.
keyCharacteristics: Dark-only, near-black ground (#09090b) with no light-mode counterpart
Tonal ladder for depth; effectively no shadow vocabulary
Hairline borders at rgba(255,255,255,0.06) as the primary edge
One mint accent (#00e599) carrying both brand and live-state signal
Three-typeface system: Clash Grotesk display, Satoshi body, JetBrains Mono label and code
Real product screenshots as the only imagery

rules.name: The Readable Floor Rule
rules.body: Never dim text with an opacity modifier. text-muted-foreground/50 and its siblings bottomed out at 1.68:1 against deep. Tertiary text uses the muted-dim token, the dimmest step that still clears AA on every surface in the ladder.

rules.name: The Single Voice Rule
rules.body: Mint is the only chromatic color in the system. Adding a second hue — a blue for "info", an amber for "warning", a purple for anything — breaks the darkroom. If a state needs distinguishing, use the tonal ladder, opacity, or type weight, not a new hue.

rules.name: The Brand Color Rule
rules.body: Mint is the brand color, not a rationed signal, and it may carry real presence across a surface: CTAs, eyebrows, active states, and live indicators, but also borders, hover treatments, tinted panels, icon accents, rules, and washes used for visual interest. Use it wherever it strengthens recognition. The one constraint that still binds is contrast — mint text or iconography must clear WCAG AA against whatever surface it lands on, which in practice means full-strength #00e599 on deep or surface, not mint-on-mint-wash at small sizes.

rules.name: The No Light Mode Rule
rules.body: :root and .dark are deliberately identical. Do not introduce a light palette, and do not write components that branch on theme. next-themes is present for infrastructure reasons, not as a design affordance.

rules.name: The Mono Means Machine Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono is reserved for things the machine said or things you type at it: commands, code, version numbers, file paths, frame captions, and status chips. Never use mono for marketing prose, headings, or button labels just for texture.

rules.name: The Tighten As You Grow Rule
rules.body: Letter-spacing decreases as type size increases (-0.02em at title, -0.025em at headline, -0.03em at display). Default tracking on a 4.5rem headline is the single fastest way to make this system look generic.

rules.name: The Eyebrow Pairing Rule
rules.body: A .mono-label eyebrow precedes a display or headline. It is never used alone, never in body copy, and never in a color other than mint.

rules.name: The Fixed Chrome Rule
rules.body: The nav is 56px, fixed, at z-50, with bg-[#09090b]/80 and backdrop-blur-xl. Any anchored heading needs scroll-margin-top of at least 6rem (7rem on desktop) so section links do not land under it.

rules.name: The Ladder, Not The Drop Rule
rules.body: When something needs to feel raised, move it up the tonal ladder and brighten its border. Do not reach for a black drop shadow — there is no box-shadow scale in this system and introducing one would flatten the darkroom into a generic dark card UI.

rules.name: The Border Brightens Rule
rules.body: Interactive elevation reads through the edge: hairline 0.06 at rest -> 0.12 on hover -> 0.20 on active or focused controls, usually paired with a surface -> surface-2 background step.

rules.name: The 12px Ceiling Rule
rules.body: No radius above 12px except intentional pills (full). Larger radii read as consumer-app friendliness, which is a confirmed anti-reference.

rules.name: The Reveal, Don't Perform Rule
rules.body: Motion exists to bring content into place, once. No looping animation, no scale-on-hover, no bounce or spring overshoot. The system contains no infinite animation at all; the hero video is the one continuous moving element, and it ships with a pause control.

rules.name: The Reduced Motion Is Real Rule
rules.body: MotionProvider wraps the app in <MotionConfig reducedMotion="user">, the single gate for every Framer animation — CSS alone cannot stop them, since Framer animates through JS. The global prefers-reduced-motion block additionally clamps CSS durations. This is a stated WCAG 2.2 AA commitment, not a nicety.

dos: Do build depth with the tonal ladder — deep -> surface -> surface-2 — and let the hairline border sharpen the step rather than create it.
Do open every quoted piece of machine output with the frame chrome bar: hairline, 11px uppercase mono caption, deep fill.
Do pair a mint .mono-label eyebrow with each section heading; it is the system's most recognizable signature.
Do tighten letter-spacing as type scales up (-0.02em -> -0.025em -> -0.03em).
Do keep imagery to real product captures — the TUI screenshots and overview video are the only imagery this system uses, and they are genuine.
Do gate every GSAP effect behind useReducedMotion() and keep focus rings visible.
Do use mint freely as the brand color — CTAs, eyebrows, active states, borders, hovers, washes, and accents — subject only to AA contrast where it carries text or iconography.
donts: Don't introduce a second chromatic hue. One accent, no exceptions — use tone, opacity, or weight to differentiate instead.
Don't add a box-shadow scale. The Accent Glow is the only shadow token; raised means one step up the ladder.
Don't build a light mode or branch components on theme. :root and .dark are identical by design.
Don't exceed a 12px radius outside deliberate pills.
Don't set marketing prose, headings, or button labels in JetBrains Mono for texture. Mono means machine.

Don't drift toward the confirmed anti-references: gradient meshes, glowing orbs, aurora blurs, or gradient text (generic dark SaaS); frosted decorative panels (glassmorphism); mascots, illustrations, or pastels (consumer app); stock photography, abstract 3D, or logo walls (enterprise stock).
Don't add looping, bouncing, or scale-on-hover motion. Reveal once and stop.
